# Inventory Rebalancing Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Inventory Rebalancing Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 22 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, the proposed planning connections and the channel; document blocked paths rather than bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the ERP, warehouse and transportation systems, Power BI and Teams, each with a dedicated least-privilege reference. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare supply-chain, inventory, procurement and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Execution authority | Have the planning owner name who authorizes movement and policy changes before real inventory data replaces the snapshot. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain planning owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Facility utilization, forecast-relative imbalance, below-reorder positions and planning cost by facility Establish the shared starting view and manual reconciliation effort before attributing faster planning decisions to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Facility | Measurement period | Utilization | Positions below reorder point | Material imbalances | Holding cost | Decision owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain planning owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Supply chain planning owner | Approve planning scope, review routes and production success measures. |
| ERP/WMS system owners | Authorize any reservation, transfer, reorder, return or policy change that a recommendation implies. |
| Inventory, warehouse, finance and transportation reviewers | Review proposed transfers and cost trade-offs before any decision. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Upload the two complete reviewed knowledge files and four skills with exact parity; remove web search and record Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any planning connection is approved. |
| Supply chain connection owners | Approve ERP, warehouse, transportation, Power BI and Teams access through dedicated, verified connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check IR-01 through IR-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft after confirming knowledge parity and cost routing. |
| Operations owner | Own monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route action requests to ERP/WMS owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for planning have named agreement.
- [ ] The planning owner records facility pressure, imbalance and planning cost before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/inventory-rebalancing/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and confirm blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and publisher prefix for the planning build are recorded before a build lane is chosen.
- [ ] The customer approves the sign-in requirement, audience and least-privilege scopes for inventory and cost data before any connection is bound.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/inventory-rebalancing/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/inventory-rebalancing/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/inventory-rebalancing/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/inventory-rebalancing/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Inventory Manual Build
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction changes
5. Remove default web search
6. Open the knowledge uploader
7. Upload synthetic inventory records
8. Upload cost and review rules
9. Verify both complete knowledge files
10. Open the SKILL.md uploader
11. Add inventory snapshot
12. Add rebalance recommendation
13. Add transfer planning
14. Add cost analysis
15. Confirm Claude Sonnet 4.6
16. Audit four skills and two knowledge files
17. Open a fresh Preview conversation
18. Pass corrected capacity review
19. Pass imbalance review
20. Pass transfer plan
21. Pass cost routing and total cost
22. Verify Draft and do not publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: IR-01, IR-02, IR-03, IR-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the smoke test calls `InventoryRebalancingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] Both knowledge uploads are the complete reviewed files, byte-identical to the source, with four skills and the confirmed model.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator decides each case; an annotated visual checkpoint does not replace it.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before inventory, cost or forecast data is shown. Request only the scopes that approved ERP, warehouse and reporting sources need. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or another approved ERP inventory source

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or another approved ERP inventory source — read:** Bind read-only inventory and demand data through a dedicated connection reference.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or another approved ERP inventory source:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or another approved ERP inventory source:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or another approved ERP inventory source:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no reorder point or policy; that needs approved tools and authorized owners. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a proposal and name the ERP/WMS owner gate; no side effect occurs.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved warehouse and transportation management systems

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain connection owners

1. **Bind Approved warehouse and transportation management systems — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any movement workflow behind ERP/WMS owner approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved warehouse and transportation management systems:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved warehouse and transportation management systems:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved warehouse and transportation management systems:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Say that the SKU and facility are not in the synthetic snapshot instead of guessing. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so instead of guessing; never substitute another record.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Power BI

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain connection owners

1. **Bind Power BI — read:** Query approved datasets read-only with the connector's query actions.

2. **Identity for Power BI:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Power BI:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Power BI:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Say that the SKU and facility are not in the synthetic snapshot instead of guessing. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so instead of guessing; never substitute another record.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Gate any Teams review or approval card behind the accountable owners.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Propose only; state that no inventory has been reserved, picked, shipped or moved, and name the ERP/WMS owner gate. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, reservation or movement succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain connection owners

Create read tools with dedicated connection references first; keep reservation, movement, reorder, return, disposition and policy tools unavailable until approved.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Read tools use dedicated connection references; action tools stay unavailable in the recommendation-only build.
- [ ] No lookup, reservation or movement is reported unless an approved production tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test the approved deployment with planning and denied identities; a maker's working connection does not prove other users' access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; the synthetic tolerance and classification are pilot conventions, not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations name the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact planning assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked planning corpus | All four cases, IR-01 through IR-04, return every required marker and no forbidden phrase. |
| Manual inventory and parity | Two complete knowledge files byte-identical to the reviewed source, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools. |
| Inventory action boundary | Any reservation, pick, shipment, transfer, reorder, return, liquidation or policy-change claim is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reusable captures show a positive deterministic anchor and no blocker; reshoot-required captures stay withheld. |
| Release state | Both validated agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain planning owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain planning owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation from the approval owner.
- [ ] The approved planning audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, misrouted cost questions, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Recovery is rehearsed with a restore path supported for the planning environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, knowledge use, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
